subject: Post-call: Searchlytics embedding health & next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.inference>
To: Eli Roberts <eli@searchlytics.ai>; Kira Tanaka <kira@searchlytics.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-08-07T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Searchlytics embedding health & next steps

Eli / Kira — thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the concrete next steps we agreed on: 

1) Goals we heard
- Improve semantic search recall on long-form docs (customer support KB)
- Reduce false positives for near-duplicate detection (high precision for top-3 results)
- Keep embedding unit costs predictable under peak indexing loads

2) Current environment notes (from call)
- ~2M documents, avg length ~1.2k tokens; you do nightly incremental indexing
- Today using a 768-d embedding model; you’ve observed drift in query performance for new content categories

3) Proposed evaluation plan (short list)
- Baseline models to benchmark: redwood-embed-512-v2 (quantized), semantic-lite-384, and a higher-dim 1024 prototype for recall tests
- Metrics: recall@5, MRR@10, median cosine similarity for positives, dimensionality cost (bytes per vector), and inference token/second throughput
- Prompt & dataset: we’ll run a seeded eval on the 500-sample holdout you shared; include 100 hard negatives we’ll generate together

4) Deliverables from Redwood (we’ll send)
- Eval report with recall/MRR curves and dimensionality cost tradeoffs (PDF)
- Notebook + instructions to reproduce locally (gist/Drive)
- Suggested prompt sets for reranking and query expansion (CSV)

Next steps (action items):
- Aditya: upload initial eval run and report by Monday (08/09) — includes recommended model (single best pick) + an alternative for low-cost mode
- Marissa: share prompt sets and hard-negative generation scripts (attached)
- Eli / Kira: confirm the 500-sample holdout and provide S3 path for the full 2k sample if we want broader runs

Attachments: we included a short sample set and the prompt seed file referenced on the call.

Thanks again, talk soon —
Aditya

--

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
To: Eli Roberts <eli@searchlytics.ai>, Kira Tanaka <kira@searchlytics.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.inference>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-08-08T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Searchlytics embedding health & next steps — eval details and model picks

Hi Eli / Kira — following up with the technical run plan and initial model recommendations. Attaching the three artifacts we mentioned.

Summary of our preliminary findings (from quick dry run on your 500-sample):
- redwood-embed-512-v2 (quantized): best cost/recall balance — recall@5 = 0.78, MRR@10 = 0.62, median positive cosine = 0.84. Index size ~256 MB for the sample extrapolated to ~1.0TB for full corpus (est).
- semantic-lite-384: lower index size (~0.75x) and slightly faster embedding latency, recall@5 = 0.73, MRR@10 = 0.58 — good for low-cost mode.
- proto-sem-1024 (experimental): highest recall (recall@5 = 0.83) but 2.1x index size and 1.8x inference cost — recommended only if recall is primary KPI.

Important notes on drift & dimensionality: 
- We observed a category shift in the last-month documents (long-form release notes) that reduces near-neighbor precision — recommends quarterly drift scans using the same seed eval set + automated hard-negative mining.
- Dimensionality increases help recall but come with storage and latency costs; we’ve included a simple cost model in the report showing estimated $/month for different dims at your scale.

Attached artifacts (zipped in Drive link and included as light PDF):
- searchlytics_eval_report_v1.pdf — full metrics, plots (recall curves, MRR, latency boxplots)
- prompt_set_seed_0416.csv — recommended query transforms and reranking prompts
- sample_docs_500.jsonl — holdout sample we used for the run

Reproducibility + next steps
- Repro notebook: https://gist.github.com/redwood/adapt-embed-eval-notebook (includes kernel, seeds)
- If you want us to run a full 2k sample we can queue a broader eval — estimate 48 hours for full runs across the three candidate models

Proposed timeline
- You confirm S3 path (Eli) — today
- We run full 2k evaluation and share final recommendation + cost model — by Tue 08/11 (if you give the green light)
- Follow-up call to review results and procurement options — propose Wed 08/12 10am PT

Happy to adjust.

Thanks —
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
